docs.title: 13. Security — summary
docs.text: Surface Measure Human auth Google OIDC + PKCE, JWKS/nonce, hd restriction, rotating refresh Cloud credentials OIDC workload by default: tokens signed per run/phase, trust policies on claims, session name = run_id (CloudTrail ↔ Stackd audit). Static = fallback OIDC signing key KMS or encrypted volume (oidc_signing_keys §3.11), rotation with overlap, short token TTL. sub wildcard allowed only on the stack segment; never on tier nor phase (§10.3) Static secrets AES-256-GCM, write-only, decrypted at claim, masked in the logs Hooks platform hooks not bypassable by PR; repo hooks without sensitive_env nor cloud credentials, with an allowlisted env, a masked plan.json, and no saved plan, tfvars, OIDC token file or repo token on disk while they run; the agent's STACKD_* settings reach no hook nor tofu; masking of sensitive values in their stdout; the process group killed when the hook exits, or past its 10 min timeout; a failing fail check stops the job at any stage (§8.3). Not implemented yet: repo hooks forbidden at the *_apply stages on tier=prod (pending a decision), execution in the run's container (§7.4) Mocks apply forbidden by default (allow_mock_apply=false), badge, audit mock_consumed External secrets provider bootstrap credential AES-256-GCM write-only (secret_sources.bootstrap_secret_encrypted §15.1); live values fetched at claim, never persisted, masked; fallback value (static or break-glass override) forbids apply by default (allow_fallback_apply=false), badge, audit secret.fallback_used (§15) Workers revocable tokens, no incoming port, labels (isolated prod pool); tool binaries verified by checksum/signature (§7.4, supply-chain) — not implemented yet (the runner images verify their binary at build; the agent runs the one on its PATH) State S3 SSE-KMS via API only; per-job state tokens scoped ro (proposed runs, read-only commands) / plan (lock, never write) / rw (apply, mutating command, import session), refused once their run is terminal; handed to tofu only, as TF_HTTP_* env (§11.2); audited force-unlock Saved plans the reviewed plan.tfplan is AES-256-GCM-encrypted by the API (AAD bound to its S3 key), served only to the run's apply job, applied as-is (never re-planned), deleted on any terminal state (§7.3, §11.3) Outbound notifications https only; the host must resolve to public addresses only; the POST dials the vetted IP (Host/SNI/certificate stay on the hostname), ignores env proxies (HTTPS_PROXY…) by design, never follows redirects Apply permissions tier per env × allowed_tiers set per user (§2.4, configurable catalog, non-linear); distinct can_destroy; double lock with the OIDC trust policy on the tier name Protected envs autodeploy forbidden and 4-eyes (also automatic on a tier flagged requires_four_eyes, e.g. prod), never bypassed (cascade included); the right to apply comes from the tier, not from protected Proposed runs plan-only, state RO, mocks allowed; secrets not injected: repo code runs inside tofu (§7.4), and a pull request's has not been reviewed. The claim drops every sensitive variable, of either kind, and every external secret reference (§15, not even fetched) — so nothing of them is in sensitive_env, the tfvars, mask_values or the run's variable_provenance. One the plan needs gets no value, never a stand-in: tofu uses the variable's default in the repo, or fails with No value for required variable. Kept, as a plan needs them: the plan role's OIDC credentials (read-only by design, §10.3 — scope it so), the ro state token (the state itself is readable: it can hold secrets of its own), the repo token to clone (it reaches neither tofu nor a hook, §8.3). A drift run (§19), a proposed run of the env's last applied commit, keeps the secrets. Specified, not implemented — pending a decision: a per-environment opt-in giving proposed runs the secrets Webhooks HMAC SHA-256 (secret per repo, stacks.webhook_secret_encrypted §3.1), anti-replay 5 min Sessions access JWT 15 min in Bearer header; refresh httpOnly SameSite=Strict + CSRF double-submit, rotation with reuse detection → family revocation (§2.5) Encryption at rest AES-256-GCM, random 96-bit nonce per value, never reused (§1) Rate limiting Google callback + /auth/refresh, /webhooks/github, discover-inputs: per-IP token buckets, per replica (§20.3). Worker register/claim are not throttled yet; hardening Phase 7 Audit append-only at the DB level (INSERT-only role + anti-update/delete trigger §6.1), denormalized, transactional, 2 years

docs.title: 14. Tests — minimal strategy
docs.text:
• API unit tests: transitions (can_apply per tier including apply-everywhere-except-prod, can_destroy, auto 4-eyes on a requires_four_eyes tier or a protected env and its human-triggerer-only scope, mock-apply blocking, warn → forced confirmation), 6-layer variable resolution + provenance (space-scoped attachments), a proposed run's claim payload carrying no secret (a tracked or drift run's still does), hook merging (platform→repo order; the exclusion of *_apply repo hooks on prod once decided, §8.3), check results kept with their stage across the plan and apply jobs (a job failing on no check included, its warnings audited), an after_apply failure recording outputs and clearing drift without cascading, cycle detection, multi-parent cascade (once built, §9.2), mock resolution (real > mock > error), signature/claims of workload tokens (tier segment in the sub, wildcard limited to the stack segment), Google id_token validation, refresh rotation + reuse detection → family revocation.
  • Integration: Postgres testcontainers; concurrent claim → only one wins, the loser catches 23505 and re-polls; HTTP backend with real tofu + Garage; log idempotency; masking of sensitive values (tfvars + env) in a hook's stdout; after_plan hook that reads plan.json; WS fan-out via LISTEN/NOTIFY; single execution of a periodic task under advisory lock with 2 replicas; AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity against a mock STS (moto).
  • E2E: the live compose stack + fixture repos (built-in terraform_data, no provider) → on a throwaway copy of the demo graph, a 2-stack cascade with mocks (mocked plan → upstream apply → real cascade), the role/mock gates, and the run.confirmed audit actor (DEV §7).
  • Agent: exit codes (a plan only on 0/2) and the plan JSON failing closed, secret masking and the masked plan.json, hooks at every stage and from both sources (fail stops the job, warn goes on, the timeout kills the process group, a background process dies with its hook), what a repo hook can read (no saved plan, tfvars, OIDC token file or repo token; an allowlisted env), the STACKD_*-free env of tofu and platform hooks, saved-plan upload and fail-closed apply, commit pinning, the TF_HTTP_* backend env (tofu only), the command time budget from cred_phase, token encoding in clone URLs, writing the OIDC token and exporting the env vars.

docs.title: 15. External secret sources (post-MVP)
docs.text: Status: post-MVP, additive. This section extends the variable model (§3.3), the claim build (§7.2) and the security model (§13). It reuses the mock apply-gate pattern (§9.3) verbatim — read it first; everything here is the same shape applied to externally-sourced secrets instead of mocked outputs.

docs.title: 15.1 Goal and model
docs.text:
A sensitive variable can carry its value by reference to an external secrets manager instead of storing the value in Stackd. At claim build the platform resolves the reference to a live value, injects it into the job exactly like any other sensitive variable, and never persists it. This is a security upgrade over a stored value_encrypted: no secret at rest in our DB, automatic rotation, single revocable bootstrap credential per source.

The provider is abstracted — Proton Pass is the first concrete implementation, others (HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager, 1Password Service Accounts, Doppler, Infisical) plug into the same interface.

New table secret_sources (scoped per space, like cloud_integrations §3.10):

CREATE TABLE secret_sources (
    id                        uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
    space_id                  uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES spaces(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name                      text NOT NULL,
    provider                  secret_provider NOT NULL,   -- enum: proton_pass | vault | aws_secrets_manager | ...
    config                    jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',-- non-sensitive: e.g. proton {server,vault_scope}; vault {address,mount,auth}
    bootstrap_secret_encrypted bytea NOT NULL,            -- AES-256-GCM, write-only: Proton PAT / AI Access Token, Vault token, ...
    created_by_user_id        uuid REFERENCES users(id),
    created_at                timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at                timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (space_id, name)
);

bootstrap_secret_encrypted follows the §1 encryption-at-rest rule and is never returned by the API (write-only, like stacks.webhook_secret_encrypted).

Variable extension (variables, §3.3) — a third value source alongside value / value_encrypted:

ALTER TABLE variables ADD COLUMN secret_source_id          uuid REFERENCES secret_sources(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT;
ALTER TABLE variables ADD COLUMN secret_ref                text;   -- provider locator, e.g. Proton "pass://vault/item/field"
ALTER TABLE variables ADD COLUMN secret_fallback_mode      secret_fallback NOT NULL DEFAULT 'error';  -- error | static | break_glass
ALTER TABLE variables ADD COLUMN secret_fallback_encrypted bytea;  -- AES-256-GCM, only for mode=static
-- exactly one value source; a referenced variable is implicitly sensitive
ALTER TABLE variables ADD CONSTRAINT variables_one_value_source CHECK (
    (value IS NOT NULL)::int
  + (value_encrypted IS NOT NULL)::int
  + (secret_source_id IS NOT NULL)::int = 1
);
-- ON DELETE RESTRICT: a source in use can't be dropped out from under live variables.

A variable with secret_source_id is treated as sensitive=true regardless of the flag.

docs.title: 15.2 Resolution order (real > fallback > error)
docs.text:
At claim build (build_job_payload, §7.2), reference variables resolve after the existing layered resolution (§3.4), by calling the provider:

  1. Provider reachable, secret found → use the live value. variable_provenance[name] = "secret:{source_name}". No audit event on success (would be noisy — successes are implicit in the run; only failures and fallbacks are audited).
  2. Provider unavailable / timeout / not-found → apply secret_fallback_mode:
  3. error (default) → the claim resolution fails: the run transitions to failed with reason secret_unavailable:{var}; the claim returns no job and the worker re-polls. Fail-closed.
  4. static → use secret_fallback_encrypted (the operator-chosen value). Sets run.used_secret_fallback = true, provenance secret_fallback:{source_name}, audit secret.fallback_used.
  5. break_glass → no stored value: the run can only proceed if the trigger carried an inline override (see §15.4). Without one it behaves like error.

This is the same real > mock > error precedence as §9.3, with "fallback" in the middle slot.

A provider fetch has a short timeout (default 10 s); a slow source counts as unavailable. Resolved values are never cached to disk or DB — caching would re-introduce a secret at rest; an optional in-process memoisation lives only for the duration of one claim build.

docs.title: 15.3 Where resolution runs
docs.text:
v1: API-side. The platform resolves references during claim build and injects the live value into the existing payload fields — sensitive_env / tfvars_json — and the literal into mask_values (§5.1). No worker or claim-payload schema change: a resolved reference is indistinguishable downstream from a stored sensitive variable. The bootstrap credential stays on the API host and is never shipped to a worker. For Proton Pass this means the API host runs pass-cli (headless, authenticated by the source's PAT / AI Access Token); for Vault/ASM it is a plain HTTPS call.

Future: worker-side (mirrors OIDC→STS, §10.4) — ship {provider, config, scoped_token, secret_ref} in the claim and let the worker fetch locally, so the value never transits the API. Deferred: it widens bootstrap-credential exposure to every worker and complicates the fallback path, for a marginal gain over the masked API-side flow. Noted here so the payload contract can grow compatibly.

docs.title: 15.4 Break-glass override (operator-supplied value)
docs.text:
When a source is down and the operator must ship anyway, the run trigger accepts an inline override (it is never stored, used for that run only):

POST /api/v1/environments/{id}/runs
  { ..., "secret_overrides": { "<variable_name>": "<value>" } }
  • Permission: supplying an override is an apply-affecting bypass → requires can_apply(user, env) (§2.4). It is rejected unless the targeted variable's secret_fallback_mode = break_glass (a source must opt in to being overridable).
  • The override value is injected like a sensitive variable, added to mask_values, and sets run.used_secret_fallback = true, provenance secret_override:{source_name}.
  • Audit secret.fallback_overridden, context = {variable, source, run_id} — the value itself is never written to the audit context (§6.1).

No new run state is introduced: break-glass reuses the trigger path, so transition() legality (invariant) is untouched.

docs.title: 15.5 Apply gate (mirrors §9.3)
docs.text:
A value produced by any fallback is not the real secret (it may be stale or operator-chosen), so it must not reach prod silently:

ALTER TABLE runs         ADD COLUMN used_secret_fallback bool NOT NULL DEFAULT false;
ALTER TABLE environments ADD COLUMN allow_fallback_apply bool NOT NULL DEFAULT false;

confirm_run() enforces, in the same place as the mock gate:

if run.used_secret_fallback and not env.allow_fallback_apply:
    raise ProblemException(409, "Apply disabled",
        "This run resolved a secret via fallback (allow_fallback_apply is off).")

The UI shows a provenance badge on any value sourced from a fallback (DESIGN — same treatment as the mock badge). Plan of a used_secret_fallback run is always allowed; only apply is gated.

docs.title: 15.6 Audit taxonomy additions (extends §6.2)
docs.text:
secret_source.created / secret_source.updated / secret_source.deleted / secret_source.token_rotated
secret.fallback_used          -- static fallback consumed (provider was down)
secret.fallback_overridden    -- operator supplied a break-glass value

A run failed because a reference could not resolve and no fallback applied is audited as run.apply_failed with context reason: secret (§6.2), not by a dedicated secret.* action.

Successful live resolutions are intentionally not audited (volume); the run's variable_provenance already records secret:{source} per variable.

docs.title: 15.7 Proton Pass binding
docs.text:
• provider = proton_pass; config = {server?, vault_scope?}; bootstrap credential = a Proton Personal Access Token or AI Access Token, scoped to the relevant vault/items (no account password). secret_ref uses Proton's URI form pass://vault/item/field.
  • Integration runs pass-cli on the resolver host (API for v1); the binary must be present in the API image and is verified by checksum (supply-chain, §7.4).
  • The Proton end-to-end model is preserved: decryption happens client-side via the token, Stackd only ever holds the (encrypted-at-rest) token and the reference, never the user's master key.

docs.title: 15.8 Invariants preserved
docs.text:
1. Secrets never logged nor returned in clear (invariant §13.3): live value, static fallback and break-glass override all enter mask_values; bootstrap_secret_encrypted and secret_fallback_encrypted are write-only.
  2. Every mutating action audited in the same transaction (§6.3): source CRUD and fallback events.
  3. A non-real value cannot be applied silently (§9.3 parity): used_secret_fallback × allow_fallback_apply.
  4. Run state only changes through transition() (invariant §4.2): no new state; failure path uses → failed, break-glass uses the normal trigger path.

docs.title: 16. Plan review — comments & highlights (post-MVP)
docs.text: Status: post-MVP, additive. Turns the approval gate into a collaborative review: an open discussion thread on a run, with comments optionally anchored to a part of the plan. Built on existing substrate — immutable run logs (the anchor target), LISTEN/NOTIFY (live updates, §5.3), the approval gate (§4). No run-state change; transition() is untouched.

docs.title: 16.1 Model
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE run_comments (
    id                  uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
    run_id              uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    parent_id           uuid REFERENCES run_comments(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,  -- thread reply
    author_user_id      uuid REFERENCES users(id),
    author_email        text,            -- denormalized, readable if the user is later removed
    body                text NOT NULL,
    anchor              jsonb,           -- NULL = general comment; else a polymorphic anchor (§16.2)
    resolved_at         timestamptz,
    resolved_by_user_id uuid REFERENCES users(id),
    created_at          timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    edited_at           timestamptz
);

Comments are per run — each plan is a distinct artifact, so a new run starts a fresh discussion.

docs.title: 16.2 Anchors (polymorphic)
docs.text:
An anchor pins a comment to a part of the plan. Two kinds (a comment with no anchor is a general thread):

// v1 — a range of plan log lines (the rendered, already-masked plan output)
{ "kind": "plan_line", "phase": "planning", "seq": 3, "line_start": 12, "line_end": 14,
  "snippet": "~ aws_s3_bucket.logs" }
// v2 — a Terraform resource address (from the structured plan.json)
{ "kind": "resource", "address": "aws_s3_bucket.logs", "action": "update" }

The plan_line anchor targets run_logs ((run_id, phase, seq) is immutable and idempotent, §5.2), so the anchor is stable for the life of the run. The snippet is copied from the masked log line (run_logs.lines[].msg), so an anchor can never carry a secret (invariant §13.3). resource anchors (v2) require serving the structured plan; the column is polymorphic so v2 needs no migration.

Rendering: plan_line threads render inline in the log viewer, directly under their line (progressive, line-level review — like PR-review comments), with a hover affordance per line to open an inline composer. General (unanchored) and resource threads live in a separate Discussion panel.

docs.title: 16.3 API
docs.text:
/api/v1/runs/{run_id}/comments — listing & posting are open to any authenticated user (collaboration, reader+); editing a body is author-only; resolving a thread needs the author or role ∈ {approver, admin}; deleting needs the author or admin.

Method Path Who Effect GET /comments any auth list (oldest first; replies carry parent_id) POST /comments any auth create {body, anchor?, parent_id?} PATCH /comments/{id} author / approver edit body (author) and/or resolved (author or approver+) DELETE /comments/{id} author / admin delete (cascades replies)

Every create/edit/delete/resolve emits a light pg_notify('run_<id>', …) (§5.3) so the run page's existing WS subscription invalidates ["run-comments", run_id] and the thread updates live.

docs.title: 16.4 Interaction with the gate
docs.text: Advisory at v1: the run page shows the count of open (unresolved) threads next to the Confirm button; it does not block. (can_apply and the §9.3/§15.5 gates are untouched.) A future opt-in env flag could make confirm require all threads resolved — deliberately deferred.

docs.title: 16.5 Invariants preserved
docs.text:
1. No run-state change — comments are a side record; transition() (invariant §4.2) is untouched.
  2. Snippets come from already-masked log lines, so no secret leaks (invariant §13.3).
  3. Live updates reuse LISTEN/NOTIFY (§5.3) — no new transport.

docs.title: 17. In-app notification center (post-MVP)
docs.text: Status: post-MVP, additive. The inbound counterpart to the outbound Slack/webhook outbox (§5/notifications): a per-user inbox surfaced as a bell in the UI. Side records only — no run-state change (transition() untouched), live over the existing LISTEN/NOTIFY transport (§5.3).

docs.title: 17.1 Model & events
docs.text:
user_notifications (per user): user_id, kind, run_id?, comment_id?, context jsonb, read_at?, created_at. kind ∈ approval_request | run_finished | run_failed | comment_reply | mention. Each row is created in the same transaction as its trigger:

  • transition() (§4.2): → unconfirmed fans out approval_request to every eligible approver — the users who pass can_apply on the env (§2.4), evaluated with their effective space membership (members of the env's space, instance admins included); a destroy run additionally requires can_destroy; excluding the triggerer. A terminal state notifies the run's human triggerer (run_finished / run_failed).
  • comment create (§16): a reply notifies the root author; @mention tokens (matched against a user's email local-part or full email) notify the mentioned users. Never the author. The composer offers @ autocomplete from GET /users/mentionable (a minimal directory readable by any auth), inserting @<email-local-part> so it resolves against the parser.

docs.title: 17.2 Live delivery — private per-user channel
docs.text: notify() emits pg_notify('user_<uid>', …) alongside the row. The WS hub maps a user:<id> subscription to user_<id> only for the connecting user's own id (channel_for(sub, user_id), §5.3) — the feed is private; you cannot listen on someone else's signals. The bell subscribes to its own channel and invalidates the ["notifications"] query on any signal (no payload trusted).

docs.title: 17.3 API
docs.text: GET /api/v1/notifications (current user, newest first, capped) ; POST /api/v1/notifications/read ({ids?} — omit to mark all of the user's unread as read). Opening the bell marks all read.

docs.title: 17.4 Invariants preserved
docs.text:
1. No run-state change — notifications are a side record; transition() (invariant §4.2) untouched.
  2. Same-txn write (invariant §6.3 spirit): a rolled-back trigger emits no notification (NOTIFY is transactional).
  3. The per-user channel is access-scoped to self; the WS payload is a content-free signal (§5.3).

docs.title: 18. VCS feedback loop — PR comment + commit status (post-MVP)
docs.text: Status: shipped (Phase A). Closes the review loop: a PR shows the plan result in GitHub — a commit status + one PR comment edited in place. Auth: PAT (the stack's repo_secret), not a GitHub App. A VCS post-back is a side-effect of transition(), never a source of truth: a VCS outage leaves the run correct. GitHub App (bot identity + Checks API) is deferred to Phase I.

docs.title: 18.1 Model
docs.text: runs (add): pr_number int? (the PR that spawned a proposed run), vcs_provider text? ('github' — enum-by-string, gitlab/bitbucket later), vcs_comment_id bigint? (the posted PR comment, for idempotent edit), vcs_head_sha text? (PR head commit the status reports against). vcs_outbox (transactional outbox, same shape as the notification outbox §17/§5): id, run_id, to_state, attempts, created_at, sent_at?, partial index WHERE sent_at IS NULL.

docs.title: 18.2 Auth — PAT
docs.text: Reuse the stack's repo_secret (already used to clone). For post-back it must additionally carry pull_requests:write + commit statuses:write (classic repo, or a fine-grained PAT with those + contents:read). No GitHub App, no extra instance config — posts appear as the token's user. A repo_secret without write scope → post-back fails soft (run unaffected, logged).

docs.title: 18.3 Webhook ingestion (webhooks/router.py)
docs.text: On pull_request (opened/synchronize/reopened): create the proposed run as today and persist pr_number, vcs_provider='github', vcs_head_sha = pr.head.sha. On closed: best-effort transition() of the still-in-flight proposed runs for that PR to canceled (reason pr_closed).

docs.title: 18.4 Post-back (app/vcs/ — transactional outbox)
docs.text:
Enqueued on the run transition() in the SAME txn (no network I/O there — a rolled-back transition never posts); drained by the scheduler dispatcher (dispatch_vcs, advisory-locked, at-least-once with attempts cap). Only runs with vcs_provider set post back. A proposed run is plan-only and terminal at finished (never unconfirmed). Enqueued on planning, finished, failed, canceled, discarded (intermediate states elided to avoid status churn).

  • Commit status (Status API — PAT-compatible) on vcs_head_sha: planning → pending; finished → success; failed → failure; canceled|discarded → error. POST /repos/{o}/{r}/statuses/{sha} with {state, target_url=<ui>/runs/{id}, context="stackd/plan", description="+a ~c -d"}. (The richer Checks API is App-only → deferred.)
  • PR comment: one comment per run, edited in place (vcs_comment_id): the +a ~c -d summary, a mocks-block-apply note, deep link to /runs/{id}. Created on first post (POST .../issues/{pr}/comments), updated on later transitions (PATCH .../issues/comments/{id}); the returned id is persisted back on the run for idempotent edits.
  • A VCS failure never fails the run (logged, retried up to the attempts cap).

docs.title: 18.5 API
docs.text:
• POST /api/v1/webhooks/github — unchanged contract, now also persists PR metadata.
  • POST /api/v1/runs/{id}/vcs/resync (writer) — re-enqueue the post-back for the run's current state (manual recovery).

docs.title: 18.6 Invariants preserved
docs.text:
1. Post-back is a side-effect of transition(), never a source of truth; a VCS outage leaves the run correct (mirrors §17.4).
  2. Same-txn enqueue (invariant §6.3 spirit): a rolled-back transition enqueues nothing.
  3. Sensitive plan values stay masked in the comment (reuse the artifact masking, §13).

docs.title: 19. Drift detection (post-MVP)
docs.text: Status: shipped (Phase B). Detects when real infrastructure diverged from the last applied state, via a periodic read-only -refresh-only plan. Never auto-remediated — drift is surfaced (env badge + inbox), the operator decides. Reuses the proposed run machinery; no new job type.

docs.title: 19.1 Model
docs.text: environments (add): drift_status text default 'unknown' (unknown | in_sync | drifted | error), last_drift_checked_at timestamptz?, drift_run_id uuid? (the proposed run that last detected drift), drift_check_enabled bool default true. runs (add): is_drift bool default false. Config: STACKD_DRIFT_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 21600 (6h) — per-env minimum spacing. New trigger source TriggeredBy.schedule; new inbox kind drift_detected.

docs.title: 19.2 Scheduler task (detect_drift, advisory-locked like the others, §7.5)
docs.text: On the 10s loop, gated on last_drift_checked_at + interval: for each drift_check_enabled, unlocked env with no active run, bump last_drift_checked_at (so a no-op env isn't retried every tick) and — if the env has an applied commit — enqueue a read-only proposed run pinned to that commit (is_drift=true, triggered_by=schedule). An env with nothing applied stays unknown.

docs.title: 19.3 Worker & claim
docs.text: No new job type: the proposed plan runs with -refresh-only (true drift = state vs reality, not state vs code), signalled by refresh_only in the claim payload. Unlike a pull request's proposed run, a drift run gets the environment's secrets (§13): it plans the last applied commit, reviewed code that already ran with them, and refreshing needs them as much as applying did. To keep drift behind user work, the claim order-by (§7.2) sorts is_drift ascending — a queued user run is always claimed before a background drift run.

docs.title: 19.4 Outcome (applied in the run's transition() txn)
docs.text: On the drift run completing: changes → drifted (set drift_run_id, audit environment.drift_detected + fan out drift_detected to the same eligible approvers as approval_request (§17.1: can_apply with effective space membership), once per edge into drift — debounced while it stays drifted); no changes → in_sync; the plan itself failing → error. A successful apply on the env reconciles state with reality → back to in_sync, drift_run_id cleared (environment.drift_cleared).

docs.title: 19.5 API / front
docs.text: drift_check_enabled is settable on env create/update; the env out carries drift_status + last_drift_checked_at + drift_run_id. Front: a neutral drift chip (icon + label, never colour alone — DESIGN §7) on the env header, and a "drifted only" filter on the env list.

docs.title: 19.6 Invariants preserved
docs.text:
1. Drift runs are read-only and never auto-applied.
  2. One active run per env unchanged (§3.5) — a drift run is skipped when a run is already active, and yields to user runs at claim time.
  3. The env status change rides the run transition() txn — a rolled-back completion changes nothing; the notification is same-txn (§17.4).

docs.title: 20.1 Metrics — GET /metrics (Prometheus)
docs.text: Unauthenticated scrape endpoint (restrict at the network layer — it exposes only bounded counts, never secrets or tfvars). prometheus-client. Cardinality is bounded: labels are state/phase/ result only, never a run id. - stackd_runs_total{state}, stackd_queue_depth, stackd_workers_online — gauges refreshed from the DB at scrape time (cheap aggregate queries). - stackd_claim_latency_seconds — histogram, observed in claim_one (queue wait = now − created_at). - stackd_run_duration_seconds{phase} — histogram, observed at the terminal transition() (claim → terminal); phase = apply if the run was confirmed, else plan. - stackd_webhook_total{result} — counter (accepted/rejected/no_match) in the webhook handler.

docs.title: 20.2 Tracing (OpenTelemetry, OTLP)
docs.text: setup_tracing(app) wires FastAPI + SQLAlchemy instrumentation and a BatchSpanProcessor → OTLPSpanExporter only when STACKD_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set; a complete no-op otherwise (the OTel stack is imported lazily). Spans link an HTTP request → run transition → claim → worker events.

docs.title: 20.3 Guardrails
docs.text:
• Rate limiting (app/ratelimit.py): an in-process token bucket per (limiter, client IP), per-replica (no Redis in the MVP). The buckets live in an LRU hard-capped at 10 000 keys under a lock (the least recently used bucket is evicted at the cap), so memory stays bounded. Applied to auth/google/callback + auth/refresh (30/min, burst 15), webhooks/github (120/min, burst 40), and discover-inputs (10/min, burst 5). 429 problem+json when empty. /me is intentionally unthrottled (the UI polls it). Dev login is not throttled (dev-only, dropped in prod).
  • Discovery clone caps: the input-discovery clone is already --depth 1 --single-branch + 30 s-bounded; Phase H adds a post-clone size budget (STACKD_DISCOVERY_MAX_REPO_MB, default 200 → 413) and a .tf file cap (STACKD_DISCOVERY_MAX_TF_FILES, default 500 → 413).

docs.title: Invariants
docs.text: /metrics and traces never include secret values or tfvars; metrics are cardinality-bounded (label by state/phase/result, never by run id).

docs.title: TESTING.md — how Stackd is tested
docs.text: The test suite is the functional contract. This document explains the testing philosophy, how to run everything, and what each test file covers. It complements DEV.md (environment) and SPECS.md (the behaviour being verified). If a test and this doc disagree, the test wins — update the doc.

docs.title: 1. Philosophy
docs.text:
• Real Postgres, never a DB mock (CLAUDE §5). Unit/integration tests run against a real PostgreSQL 18 spun up with testcontainers; migrations are applied with Alembic before the suite. This catches what an in-memory fake never would: the one_active_run_per_env partial unique index, FOR UPDATE … SKIP LOCKED, LISTEN/NOTIFY, uuidv7(), JSONB <@ containment, cascade FKs.
  • Real AWS surfaces are mocked with moto (S3 for the state backend and the saved plans, STS for AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity). Everything else is real.
  • Three rings of confidence:
  • Unit — pure logic with no I/O (e.g. can_apply, the masker, plan-summary parsing).
  • Integration — the API exercised over HTTP via an in-process ASGI client against the real DB; a simulated worker drives runs by POSTing worker events.
  • End-to-end — the live compose stack with a real worker container executing OpenTofu, driven over HTTP. This is the non-regression contract (DEV §7).
  • No state change outside transition() and audit in the same transaction are not just runtime invariants — they're asserted (test_ws_notify, test_audit, every confirm/cascade test).

docs.title: 2. Running the tests
docs.text:
All commands go through the Taskfile:

task test     # API unit + integration (testcontainers) + front vitest
task e2e      # live end-to-end scenario (brings up the stack, seeds, runs api/e2e)
task lint     # ruff check + ruff format --check (api)

Under the hood:

Task Command Needs task test docker compose exec -T api uv run pytest then cd front && pnpm test (vitest run) compose api up, Docker for testcontainers task e2e docker compose exec -T api uv run pytest e2e -v (deps: dev) full stack + a live worker + the provisioned dev S3

task test does not run the worker suite. Run it directly — it needs no DB and no stack:

cd worker && uv run pytest

Run an API subset inside the api container:

docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.dev.yml exec -T api uv run pytest tests/test_runs.py -v
docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.dev.yml exec -T api uv run pytest tests/test_notifications.py::test_dispatcher_delivers_to_matching_targets

CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs ruff, pytest and mypy for the API, ruff and pytest for the worker, and typecheck + vitest + build for the front; e2e.yml runs the live scenario.

docs.title: pytest configuration (api/pyproject.toml)
docs.text:
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"                          # plain `async def test_*`, no decorator
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "session" # one event loop for the whole run …
asyncio_default_test_loop_scope = "session"    # … so the session-scoped engine isn't cross-loop
testpaths = ["tests"]                          # bare `pytest` only collects unit/integration
pythonpath = ["."]                             # make `app` importable from tests/ AND e2e/

testpaths = ["tests"] is why api/e2e/ is not collected by task test — it lives outside tests/ so the testcontainers conftest never applies to it (the e2e wants the live DB, not a throwaway one). task e2e points pytest at e2e explicitly.

docs.title: api/tests/conftest.py — the integration harness
docs.text:
Fixture Scope What it does _database session Starts a postgres:18 testcontainer (asyncpg driver), sets DATABASE_URL, a JWT secret, a 32-byte encryption key, STACKD_DEV_AUTH=true, STACKD_ALLOWED_DOMAINS, an moto-friendly AWS_REGION, disables the scheduler (STACKD_RUN_SCHEDULER=false) so it can't fail runs mid-assertion, then runs alembic upgrade head. _seed session, autouse Calls app.seed.seed() so the default/demo spaces and the tier catalog exist before any test. client function An httpx.AsyncClient over ASGITransport(app) (in-process, no socket). Deletes all runs before each test so the global claim queue starts clean. Enters the app lifespan context.

Tests that need the scheduler's tasks (worker loss, head polling, drift) call them directly.

docs.title: api/tests/conftest_phase2.py — run/worker helpers
docs.text: Helper Purpose login(client, persona) Dev-login as admin/alice/bob; returns an Authorization header dict. make_stack(client, h, name) POST /stacks; returns the stack id. make_env(client, h, stack_id, name, tier, *, autodeploy, protected) POST /stacks/{id}/environments; returns the env id. register_worker(client, admin, pool_name, worker_name="w1") Creates a pool, registers a worker, returns the worker's auth header. event(client, wh, job_id, name, *, phase, result) POST /worker/v1/jobs/{id}/events — the lever that drives a run through phases from a simulated worker.

docs.title: api/e2e/conftest.py — the live harness
docs.text: Fixture Difference from the unit harness http Real httpx.AsyncClient over HTTP to STACKD_E2E_BASE_URL (default http://localhost:8000) — not ASGI. Talks to the running api container, which shares Postgres with the live worker. graph Builds a throwaway copy of the seeded demo graph through the public API, as admin, in the demo space (e2e-<MMDDhhmmss>-<tag>-network / -app: same repos, tiers, settings, variable-set attachments, dependency + mock). It reads the seed straight from the DB (the API hides mock values). Teardown ends what is still active, then deletes the copy if the scenario passed; otherwise it keeps it and names it in a warning. Every run starts from never-applied environments, so the scenario is re-runnable without task reset (DEV §7).

docs.title: worker/tests/ — no conftest
docs.text: Worker tests import agent modules directly (agent.main, agent.workspace, agent.runner, agent.masking, agent.diagnostics…) and fake the API client where a job is driven end to end. No DB and no external network: the clone tests run real git against local repositories (one dials a closed loopback port, test_hook_secrets.py serves one over a loopback HTTP server). Hooks run for real (sh -c); tofu is a stand-in script, except in the one test that runs the real OpenTofu when tofu is on the PATH (skipped otherwise).

docs.title: 4. Test map (what each file covers)
docs.text: One line per file. The test names are descriptive: uv run pytest --collect-only -q lists them all. Counts in parentheses include parametrized cases and drift as tests are added — see §5.

a space membership overrides the instance tiers, role and destroy right. test_spaces.py (8) Per-space RBAC: non-members blocked on env-scoped reads, /graph and space listing scoped to memberships, grant then revoke, create = instance admin, members listing = space admin, create in an unknown space → 404. test_tiers.py (4) Tier catalog: name charset (OIDC sub safety), allowed_tiers validated, deleting a tier strips grants, a tier in use can't be deleted. test_users.py (3) User listing is admin-only; docs.title: API — end-to-end (api/e2e/, 1 scenario)
docs.text:
test_scenario.py::test_full_scenario — the DEV §7 narrative against the live stack and a real worker running OpenTofu, on the graph copy (≈2 min). It drives, in order:

  1. bob (writer) triggers network/dev → plan → unconfirmed.
  2. bob is refused at confirm (apply needs approver+); alice confirms → apply → finished.
  3. the cascade plans app/dev with the real upstream output (used_mocks=false).
  4. bob triggers app/prod before network/prod is applied → plan uses the mock (used_mocks=true).
  5. confirming the mock run is refused (409, allow_mock_apply=false); the run is discarded.
  6. bob triggers network/prod, then is refused at confirm (writer can't apply).
  7. alice confirms network/prod (approver, prod tier, 4-eyes vs bob) → finished.
  8. the cascade re-runs app/prod, now with the real output (used_mocks=false).
  9. the audit lists run.confirmed with alice@dev.local as the actor.

Every apply goes through the saved plan in S3, so the scenario needs the provisioned dev Garage. The tier gate (an approver without prod) and staleness stay manual checks (DEV §3, §7).

docs.title: Worker (worker/tests/)
docs.text: File Covers test_saved_plan.py (10) The plan job uploads the plan it showed, before the after_plan hooks; destroy runs plan with -destroy; the apply job applies exactly the saved plan, fails closed without a usable one, reports a stale plan clearly; the plan file is never written through a checked-out symlink; the API's refusal reaches the job error. test_commit_pin.py (7) An unpinned clone takes the env branch head; a pinned SHA off the default tip and a pinned ref are checked out exactly; an unknown commit fails at fetch; the plan reports its commit; an apply without a pinned commit fails closed. test_backend_env.py (12) The managed backend reaches tofu only via TF_HTTP_* (never -backend-config), with no lock address for a read-only job; inherited TF_HTTP_* dropped; unmanaged unchanged; repo hooks never get it, in plan, apply and command jobs; tofu's environment carries none of the agent's STACKD_* settings, in all three jobs. test_hook_failures.py (40) At every stage and from both sources: a fail hook fails the job at its stage, a warn one lets it finish and is reported; a failing before_apply hook stops the apply; a hook past STACKD_HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is killed and fails by its on_failure; a hook's background process is killed when the hook exits, whether it holds the hook's output or not; a job failing on no check (init, plan, plan JSON, apply, an uncaught error) reports the checks of the stages that ran; every check result is reported with its stage, in plan and apply jobs. test_hook_secrets.py (8) What a repo hook can read: no saved plan, raw plan JSON, tfvars, OIDC token file or repo token in the workspace; a masked plan.json at after_plan (platform hooks get the raw one); symlinks a repo plants never receive a secret; the clone leaves no token under .git/; repo hooks get only the allowlisted worker env, platform hooks none of the agent's STACKD_* settings; command runs still read the tfvars; the real OpenTofu end to end. test_exit_codes.py (17) A plan succeeds only on exit 0 or 2: an error, the watchdog's kill (124), a signal or any other code fails the job with the reason; token injection into HTTPS clone URLs. test_concurrency.py (3) The in-flight counter; STACKD_MAX_CONCURRENT_JOBS default and floor. test_runner_diag.py (1) A tofu diagnostic is expanded to its detail and location. test_diagnostics.py (1) The diagnostics bundle lists env var names, never values.

docs.title: Front (front/)
docs.text:
• vitest (pnpm test): StateBadge.test.tsx (label alongside color, mocked/fallback modifiers), ProvenanceBadge.test.ts (provenance parsing) and ProvenanceBadge.render.test.tsx.
  • Playwright (pnpm e2e, e2e/happy-path.spec.ts): one smoke test — dev login reaches the Stacks view — against a running dev stack (PW_BASE_URL, default http://localhost:5173). Not run by CI yet.
  • Ladle stories (pnpm ladle / pnpm ladle:build) pin the identity components visually (the DESIGN §8 contract): StateBadge, PhaseRail, ProvenanceBadge, plus BrandMark and the base UI kit.

docs.title: 5. Counts
docs.text:
Roughly 282 API tests (38 files), 184 worker tests (15 files), 1 e2e scenario and 9 front unit tests, parametrized cases included. The numbers move with every change; count them instead of trusting this page:

cd api && uv run pytest --collect-only -q | tail -1      # unit + integration
cd worker && uv run pytest --collect-only -q | tail -1

docs.title: 6. Adding a test
docs.text:
• Touching runs / permissions / cascade? Add an integration test in api/tests/ using the client fixture and the conftest_phase2 helpers, and make sure task e2e still passes (it's the core contract — CLAUDE §6).
  • A new mutating endpoint? Assert it writes an audit_event in the same transaction (invariant #2) — pattern it after test_audit / the CRUD tests.
  • Pure logic (no I/O)? A plain unit test (see test_permissions.py, worker/tests/test_masking.py).
  • Don't mock the DB. Use the real testcontainer; if you need AWS, use moto (see test_state_backend.py, test_oidc.py).
  • Isolation: the client fixture wipes runs before each test; if your test seeds rows that the global /graph or cross-space queries would surface, clean them up in a finally (see test_seed.py).

docs.title: API
docs.text:
Stackd exposes two REST surfaces under versioned prefixes:

  • /api/v1 — the human/automation API (auth, spaces, stacks, environments, variables, runs, hooks, dependencies, notifications, audit, state management, workers, health, logs).
  • /worker/v1 — the worker (agent) API: register, heartbeat, claim, events, logs, artifacts (including the saved plan the apply job downloads). Workers authenticate with a pool/worker token; humans never call this.

Outside these prefixes: the Terraform HTTP state backend (/state/v1/{env_id}, used by tofu with a per-job state token), the OIDC issuer (/.well-known/openid-configuration, /oidc/jwks), and two unauthenticated probes, /healthz and /metrics (Prometheus).

Errors follow RFC 9457 (application/problem+json).

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Human endpoints take a Bearer access token (a 15-minute JWT). In dev, get one via dev login:

TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/auth/dev/login \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"persona":"alice"}' | jq -r .access_token)
curl -s localhost:8000/api/v1/stacks -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

In production, authentication is Google OIDC (PKCE) with a rotating refresh token; mutating calls on /refresh and /logout use a CSRF double-submit token.

docs.title: Interactive reference
docs.text:
The API is FastAPI, so the full, always-current schema is served by the running instance:

  • Swagger UI — /docs (disabled when STACKD_ENV=production)
  • OpenAPI JSON — /openapi.json

docs.title: The main surface
docs.text:
A curated map, paths relative to /api/v1 unless noted (the Specification §12 is the exhaustive list):

Area Examples Auth POST /auth/dev/login (dev only), POST /auth/refresh, POST /auth/logout, GET /auth/me Spaces GET/POST /spaces, GET/PUT /spaces/{id}/members, DELETE /spaces/{id}/members/{user_id}, secret sources under /spaces/{id}/secret-sources Stacks GET/POST /stacks, GET/PATCH/DELETE /stacks/{id} (409 while a run is active), POST /stacks/{id}/check-repo Environments POST /stacks/{id}/environments, GET /environments/{id}/resolved-variables, POST /environments/{id}/refresh-head, POST /environments/{id}/discover-inputs Variables & sets variables CRUD (stack/env/set), variable sets + attachments (tier/stack/env of the set's space) Runs POST /environments/{id}/runs, /commands, /promote; GET /runs/{id}, POST /runs/{id}/confirm/discard/cancel, GET /runs/{id}/logs/plan/checks, POST /runs/{id}/vcs/resync Comments GET/POST /runs/{id}/comments, PATCH/DELETE /runs/{id}/comments/{cid} Hooks GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /stacks/{id}/hooks and /environments/{id}/hooks Dependencies dependencies CRUD, link-by-name, /outputs, /graph State GET .../state/versions, POST .../state/import-session, DELETE .../state/lock (force-unlock) Cloud cloud-integration CRUD + AssumeRole test Notifications targets: GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /stacks/{id}/notifications and /environments/{id}/notifications, plus …/{tid}/test; your in-app feed: GET /notifications, POST /notifications/read Users & tiers GET /users (admin), PATCH /users/{id} (admin), GET /users/mentionable, GET/POST /tiers, PATCH/DELETE /tiers/{id} Audit GET /audit (filters), GET /audit/export (CSV) — both admin-only Webhooks POST /webhooks/github OIDC issuer GET /.well-known/openid-configuration, GET /oidc/jwks Workers GET/POST /worker-pools, DELETE /worker-pools/{id} (admin), GET /workers, GET /queue, worker diagnostics Observability GET /health, GET /logs (admin); outside /api/v1: GET /healthz, GET /metrics WebSocket GET /api/v1/ws — live run/environment updates and your own notification feed

docs.title: Cloud credentials via OIDC
docs.text:
Stackd hands each run short-lived, per-phase cloud credentials instead of static access keys. Stackd is itself an OIDC issuer: at claim time it signs a workload token scoped to the run, and AWS exchanges that token for an IAM role via AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity. There are no static AWS keys stored anywhere.

The token subject is the basis of every trust policy:

sub = run:<tier>:<stack>:<phase>      e.g.  run:prod:core-network:apply

Plan and apply assume different roles

A plan job and an apply job get tokens with different phase segments and therefore assume different IAM roles: plan is read-only, apply is write. A PR plan physically cannot modify infrastructure. A command run gets the apply role for a mutating command (import, state rm…) and the plan role for a read-only one.

The token expires after session_duration, capped per phase: 30 min for plan, and the apply window (the apply budget + grace, 20 min by default) for apply — so apply credentials never outlive the job they were minted for.

docs.title: How the issuer works
docs.text:
Stackd exposes a standard OIDC discovery surface, RS256-signed:

GET /.well-known/openid-configuration   → issuer, jwks_uri, alg RS256
GET /oidc/jwks                          → public keys (kid, with rotation overlap)

AWS STS fetches the JWKS from these endpoints to validate the workload token.

The issuer must be publicly reachable over HTTPS

AWS STS calls /.well-known/openid-configuration and /oidc/jwks directly. The Stackd issuer URL must be reachable from AWS over HTTPS — a private-only deployment will fail every AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity. Expose it publicly, or use the provided Terraform module that registers the identity provider with its thumbprint.

docs.title: 1. Configure the cloud provider (AWS)
docs.text:
On the AWS account, create an IAM OIDC identity provider trusting the Stackd issuer, then the roles each run will assume. A provided Terraform module sets this up.

Use a separate role per phase:

  • plan_role_arn → a ReadOnly role (plus access to the state backend).
  • apply_role_arn → a scoped write role.

Each role's trust policy filters on the sub claim. The wildcard covers only the stack segment — tier and phase are always pinned:

# Trust policy of the prod APPLY role — refuses everything else
condition {
  test     = "StringLike"
  variable = "stackd.example.com:sub"
  values   = ["run:prod:*:apply"]   # any stack, but tier=prod AND phase=apply
}

Never wildcard tier or phase

A trust policy that left the tier or phase open (run:*:*:*) would cancel the double lock. The AWS-side tier filter is the second half of the apply guard: even if the API were bypassed, STS refuses to mint prod-write credentials for a non-prod token. Keep tier and phase fixed in every condition.

docs.title: 2. Attach a cloud integration to the environment
docs.text:
A cloud-integration is configured per environment (so each region can point at a different role or even a different AWS account). The resource is CRUD over:

GET|PUT|DELETE /api/v1/environments/{id}/cloud-integration

curl -s -X PUT localhost:8000/api/v1/environments/$PROD/cloud-integration -H "$AUTH" -d '{
  "provider": "aws",
  "plan_role_arn":  "arn:aws:iam::123:role/stackd-prod-plan",
  "apply_role_arn": "arn:aws:iam::123:role/stackd-prod-apply",
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "session_duration": 3600
}'

AWS is the MVP target; GCP and Azure come later.

docs.title: 3. Test it
docs.text:
A built-in AssumeRole test verifies the trust chain without launching a run:

curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/environments/$PROD/cloud-integration/test -H "$AUTH"

It signs a probe token and attempts the AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity end to end — a fast way to catch a missing identity provider, a too-narrow sub condition, or an unreachable issuer.

docs.title: What the agent injects
docs.text:
When a cloud_integration is set, the worker exports, to tofu and to platform hooks only:

AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE = <path to the token file, outside the checkout>
AWS_ROLE_ARN                = <plan_role_arn | apply_role_arn for this phase>
AWS_ROLE_SESSION_NAME       = stackd-<run_id>
AWS_REGION                  = <region, when the integration sets one>

The token file is written right before each tofu command or platform hook and deleted right after: it is never on disk while a repo hook runs.

The AWS SDK inside the providers performs the AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity natively. The session name ties every CloudTrail entry back to the run — and thus to the human who confirmed the apply.

These variables are never exported to repo hooks (a .stackd.yml pushed via PR must not be able to assume the apply role and exfiltrate). Platform hooks always get them. See Hooks.

docs.title: Fallback and coexistence
docs.text: With no cloud_integration, Stackd falls back to classic static variables (for example an aws-credentials variable set). Don't resolve both on one environment: Stackd does not warn about it yet, and a static AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID stays in tofu's environment, where the AWS SDK normally uses it before the OIDC token.

docs.title: Running commands (import, state surgery…)
docs.text:
Some operations don't fit plan → apply: importing an existing resource, removing something from state, re-tainting a resource. Stackd runs these as a command run — one allowlisted tofu/terraform subcommand executed on the worker, in the environment, with the same audit and the managed backend as any other run.

Note

This is not arbitrary shell. The worker runs <tool> <command> <args> where command is taken verbatim from an allowlist. To remove a stuck lock, use the dedicated force-unlock (UI State tab, or DELETE /api/v1/environments/{id}/state/lock) — it isn't a command.

docs.title: Allowed commands
docs.text:
Read-only (needs writer) Mutating (needs apply rights) output, show, state list, state show, validate, providers import, state rm, state mv, taint, untaint, refresh

Mutating commands change real state, so they're gated by can_apply(user, env) — the same role + tier check as approving an apply (see Runs & approvals). Read-only commands only need writer.

docs.title: Run one
docs.text:
From the UI: open an environment → the Command tab → pick a command, add arguments, run. You land on the run page with live logs.

Over the API:

# import an existing bucket into state
curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/environments/$ENV_ID/commands -H "$AUTH" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "command": "import",
  "args": ["aws_s3_bucket.logs", "my-existing-bucket"]
}'

# remove a resource from state
curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/environments/$ENV_ID/commands -H "$AUTH" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "command": "state rm", "args": ["aws_instance.old"]
}'

The response is a normal run (type: command). It flows queued → preparing → running → finished/failed, holds the one-active-run-per-env lock (no command races a plan/apply), streams logs, and uses the managed state backend.

docs.title: What it runs with
docs.text:
• The worker clones the repo at the request's commit_sha (a full SHA, a branch or a tag) or, by default, the head of the environment's branch, inits with the env's backend, then runs the subcommand — so config-aware commands like import work. No hooks run.

  • Credentials follow the command. The claim tells the worker the job's credential phase (cred_phase):

    Read-only command Mutating command cred_phase plan apply OIDC role the plan (read-only) role the apply role State token ro: reads state only, never locks (its backend has no lock address) rw: may lock and write state Token lifetime 6 h the apply window (apply budget + grace, 20 min by default) Time budget the agent's default cap (2 h) the apply budget (STACKD_APPLY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, 15 min by default)

    A mutating command killed at its budget fails with an "exceeded the …s time budget" error. If its worker disappears, the run is only reclaimed (worker_lost) after the apply window, by which time its tokens have expired — two workers never write the env's state at once. See Workers & scaling and Cloud credentials. - Audited: run.command_triggered on trigger and run.command_executed on success; a failure is run.apply_failed.

Warning

import needs to read the real resource, so the assumed role must have access to it. For an existing stack you're adopting, pair this with Importing an existing stack.

docs.text:

docs.title: Dependencies, outputs & mocks
docs.text: Environments can depend on each other and pass outputs as inputs. An upstream environment (e.g. network/dev) produces outputs; a downstream environment (e.g. app/dev) consumes them as variables. This is what lets Stackd wire a whole stack together and run it as a cascade — and what mocks let you bootstrap before the first apply ever happens.

docs.title: Declare a dependency
docs.text:
A dependency is an edge upstream env → downstream env plus a list of output_references. Each reference maps an upstream output_name (a Terraform output) to a downstream input_name (a variable, without the TF_VAR_ prefix), with an optional mock_value.

curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/environments/$APP_DEV/dependencies \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
    "upstream_env_id": "'"$NETWORK_DEV"'",
    "trigger_policy": "on_output_change",
    "references": [
      { "output_name": "network_name", "input_name": "network_name", "mock_value": "mock-network" }
    ]
  }'

Cycles are rejected at creation (422). The only structural constraint is upstream <> downstream — two environments of the same stack may depend on each other (primary/secondary region pattern). To wire same-named environments across two stacks in bulk, use the helper:

curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/stacks/$APP_STACK_ID/dependencies/link-by-name \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"upstream_stack_id": "'"$NETWORK_STACK_ID"'", "trigger_policy": "on_output_change"}'

It links each environment of the stack in the path to the same-named environment of upstream_stack_id, skipping pairs already linked and any edge that would close a cycle, and returns {"created": N} — running it twice is harmless. Add the output_references on each edge afterwards.

docs.title: How inputs resolve
docs.text:
Inputs are resolved fresh at claim time and snapshotted into resolved_inputs. The rule is real upstream output > mock > explicit error.

flowchart TD
  A[Resolve reference] --> B{Upstream output exists?}
  B -->|yes| C[Use real value]
  B -->|no| D{mock_value defined?}
  D -->|yes| E[Inject mock · used_mocks=true]
  D -->|no| F[Run fails · missing_upstream_output]

A sensitive upstream output is never stored nor propagated: a reference pointing at one is a visible config error, never a silent null.

docs.title: Mocks & the apply block
docs.text:
Mocks solve the chicken-and-egg of bootstrapping a cascade: you can plan app/dev with network_name = "mock-network" before network/dev has ever applied, just to validate config. A run that injected a mock is flagged used_mocks=true, audited as dependency.mock_consumed, and wears a violet MOCKED badge in the UI.

A mocked run cannot be applied

unconfirmed → confirmed is refused when used_mocks=true and the environment keeps the default allow_mock_apply=false. A mocked plan is for validation, not for real changes. Set allow_mock_apply=true on the environment to override. Mocked runs are never autodeployed; PR (proposed) runs use mocks freely since they are plan-only.

docs.title: Cascade
docs.text:
On a tracked apply finishing (applying → finished), Stackd parses outputs.json and upserts non-sensitive outputs into env_outputs (each with a value_hash). It then walks the outgoing edges and triggers downstream runs (type=tracked, triggered_by=dependency, sharing a run_group_id):

trigger_policy behavior never downstream is never auto-triggered always downstream triggered on every finished upstream apply on_output_change triggered only if the resolved value_hash differs from the downstream's last run

Each finished upstream apply triggers its downstream runs on its own: a downstream with two parents can run twice. Waiting for all parents of a run group, and stopping a branch when a parent fails, are specified but not implemented yet (SPECS §9.2). Only a finished apply cascades: a failed run, including one whose after_apply hook failed, triggers nothing.

Protections are never bypassed

A cascade run is routed like any other plan. It auto-confirms only on an autodeploy, unprotected environment, with no mock and no warn check; a protected downstream always stops at unconfirmed and waits for a human — see Runs & approvals.

Launch a whole subgraph at once with with_downstream: true in the trigger body; the root starts and subsequent levels follow via cascade:

curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/environments/$NETWORK_DEV/runs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"with_downstream": true}'

docs.title: Inspect
docs.text:
curl -s localhost:8000/api/v1/environments/$APP_DEV/outputs   -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
curl -s localhost:8000/api/v1/graph                            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

/graph only shows the environments and edges of the spaces you can see. There is no run-group endpoint yet: follow a cascade on the graph page, or through the downstream environments' runs (triggered_by: "dependency").

To remove an edge: DELETE /api/v1/dependencies/{id}.

docs.title: External secret sources
docs.text:
A sensitive variable can carry its value by reference to an external secrets manager instead of storing the value in Stackd. At run time the platform resolves the reference to a live value, injects it like any other sensitive variable, and never persists it.

This is a security upgrade over a stored secret: no secret at rest in Stackd's database, automatic rotation (you rotate in the manager, not here), and a single revocable bootstrap credential per source.

Provider support

Proton Pass is the first provider, via its CLI and scoped Personal Access / AI Access Tokens. The model is provider-agnostic — Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, 1Password and others plug into the same interface.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  V["variable<br/>(reference)"] -->|secret_ref| SRC["secret source<br/>(bootstrap token)"]
  SRC -->|fetch at claim time| PM["secrets manager"]
  PM -->|live value| CLAIM["worker claim payload<br/>(masked in logs)"]

Resolution precedence per reference mirrors the rule for dependency mocks — real value > fallback > error:

  1. Provider reachable → the live value is used. Provenance secret:<source>.
  2. Provider unreachable → the configured fallback applies, or the run fails closed.

The fetched value flows into the run exactly like a stored sensitive variable: it lands in the worker's tfvars/sensitive_env and the agent masks it in all logs.

docs.title: 1. Create a secret source
docs.text:
A secret source is scoped to a space and holds the machine credential used to fetch secrets. The credential is AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest and write-only — it is never returned by the API. Creating one requires the admin role.

SRC=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/spaces/$SPACE/secret-sources \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
        "name": "proton",
        "provider": "proton_pass",
        "bootstrap_secret": "<proton personal access token>"
      }' | jq -r .id)

In the UI: Stack → Secret sources → Manage secret sources.

docs.title: 2. Reference it from a variable
docs.text:
Point a variable at the source with a provider-specific locator. For Proton Pass that is a pass://vault/item/field URI. A referenced variable is implicitly sensitive.

curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/environments/$ENV/variables \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
        "kind": "terraform",
        "name": "db_password",
        "secret_source_id": "'"$SRC"'",
        "secret_ref": "pass://infra/prod-db/password"
      }'

The resolved value shows up in GET /environments/{id}/resolved-variables with provenance secret:proton (and masked, since it is sensitive).

docs.title: Fallback when the source is down
docs.text:
Each reference has a secret_fallback_mode that decides what happens if the provider is unreachable at run time:

Mode Behaviour when the source is down error (default) The run fails closed (secret_unavailable). Nothing is shipped. static A pre-stored, operator-chosen value is used. break_glass A value supplied inline at trigger time is used (see below).

docs.title: Static fallback
docs.text:
Store a value of your choice alongside the reference; it is used automatically only when the provider fails:

curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/environments/$ENV/variables \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
        "kind": "terraform",
        "name": "db_password",
        "secret_source_id": "'"$SRC"'",
        "secret_ref": "pass://infra/prod-db/password",
        "secret_fallback_mode": "static",
        "secret_fallback": "last-known-good-value"
      }'

docs.title: Break-glass override
docs.text:
For a break_glass reference, an operator supplies the value inline at trigger time. It is used only for that run, sealed AES-GCM, and never stored as a variable. Because it bypasses the real secret, it requires apply permission:

curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/environments/$ENV/runs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{ "secret_overrides": { "db_password": "manual-value" } }'

docs.title: Fallback blocks apply by default
docs.text:
A fallback value is not the real secret — it may be stale or operator-chosen. So a run that resolved any reference via fallback is flagged used_secret_fallback and cannot be applied unless the environment opts in:

curl -s -X PATCH localhost:8000/api/v1/environments/$ENV \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{ "allow_fallback_apply": true }'

This mirrors the mock apply-gate (allow_mock_apply). The plan is always allowed; only the apply is gated. In the UI the run carries a Fallback badge and the variable shows a FALLBACK: / OVERRIDE: provenance.

Warning

Leave allow_fallback_apply off on production environments. A fallback is a break-glass affordance for an outage, not a normal path — keeping it off forces a deliberate, audited opt-in before a non-live secret ever reaches prod.

docs.title: Audit
docs.text: Source management and every fallback event are audited (secret_source.created, secret_source.token_rotated, secret.fallback_used, secret.fallback_overridden). A run failed because a reference could not resolve is audited as run.apply_failed with reason: secret. The secret value itself is never written to the audit context. Successful live resolutions are not audited individually — the run's variable_provenance records secret:<source> per variable.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: Bring up a complete local Stackd in one command, log in, and drive a run from plan to apply — no Google account or AWS needed.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Docker, Task, uv, and pnpm (via corepack).

docs.title: Launch the stack
docs.text:
task dev      # generates .env + dev keys, provisions the dev S3, brings up the stack, migrates & seeds

This starts Postgres, an API, a worker, the front, and object storage (Garage), applies the migrations, and seeds a demo. Open http://localhost:5173.

Before the containers start, task dev provisions Garage (scripts/bootstrap-s3.sh, also task s3): it assigns the single-node layout, writes a generated access key into .env (S3_ACCESS_KEY / S3_SECRET_KEY, only when both are empty), and creates the stackd bucket. The API needs it from the first plan: every tracked plan with changes is saved there, encrypted, until its run ends. Every step checks before it acts, so re-running task dev is safe. See Dev environment §2.

docs.title: Log in
docs.text:
In dev, authentication is a dev login with three personas of distinct tiers — no real IdP:

Persona Role Allowed tiers Destroy admin admin dev, staging, prod ✅ alice approver dev, staging, prod ❌ bob writer dev, staging ❌

Note

bob (writer) can trigger plans but cannot approve an apply — approving requires the approver or admin role. See Runs & approvals.

docs.title: Your first run
docs.text:
The seed creates a demo-network and a demo-app stack in the demo space, each with a dev and a prod environment; demo-app consumes demo-network's output. From the UI:

  1. Open a stack → an environment → Plan. A run is created and a worker picks up its plan job.
  2. Watch the Run page: the phase rail, the plan diff, the checks, the resolved inputs with their provenance, and the live log.
  3. When it reaches unconfirmed, an approver clicks Confirm & apply. On prod, that approver must be someone other than the person who triggered the run (four-eyes), and types the environment's name to confirm. The apply runs exactly the plan you reviewed, on the commit it was made on — see Runs & approvals.

The same flow over the API:

# Dev-login as alice and capture the access token
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/auth/dev/login \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"persona":"alice"}' | jq -r .access_token)
AUTH="Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# Trigger a plan on an environment, then confirm the resulting run
curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/environments/$ENV_ID/runs -H "$AUTH" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'
curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/runs/$RUN_ID/confirm -H "$AUTH"

docs.title: Useful tasks
docs.text:
task test     # API unit + integration (real Postgres via testcontainers) + front vitest
task e2e      # the full live scenario, a real worker running OpenTofu (re-runnable)
task reset    # tear everything down (DB + Garage volumes) and start fresh; .env keeps its keys
task s3-ls    # list the dev bucket (saved plans, managed states)
task psql · task logs · task lint · task docs

A plan fails while saving the plan file

The API could not reach the dev S3. Run task s3 (idempotent), then task dev again so the api container is recreated with the key from .env.

docs.title: Hooks & .stackd.yml
docs.text: Hooks are shell steps that run at lifecycle stages around init / plan / apply. They come from two sources with very different trust levels: platform hooks (defined in the UI/API, non-bypassable) and repo hooks (defined in a .stackd.yml in your repository).

docs.title: The two sources
docs.text:
Platform hook Repo hook Defined in the UI/API, at stack or environment level a .stackd.yml file in the repo, versioned Who controls it a writer+ (audited) anyone who can push code / open a PR Purpose imposed governance — not bypassable by a PR project-specific logic (file generation, terragrunt, infracost…) Trusted with secrets yes no

Execution order at each stage: platform stack hooks → platform environment hooks → repo hooks. Put your critical security checks on the platform side, not in the repo.

docs.title: .stackd.yml
docs.text:
Place it at the root of the stack's project_root (so one repo can carry a different file per stack). Only the hooks: key is read.

version: 1
hooks:
  before_plan:
    - name: generate-locals
      command: ./scripts/gen-locals.sh
  after_plan:
    - name: infracost
      command: infracost breakdown --path plan.json --format table
      on_failure: warn          # fail | warn (default: fail)
    - name: no-destroy-prod
      command: jq -e '[.resource_changes[] | select(.change.actions | index("delete"))] | length == 0' plan.json
      on_failure: fail

Each hook is one shell command run in the checkout (cwd = project_root), with name, command and on_failure.

Stages. The plan job runs before_init, after_init, before_plan and after_plan. The apply job, a fresh clone of the reviewed commit, runs before_apply and after_apply. A command run runs no hook. plan.json exists only at after_plan.

docs.title: Failures, warnings and timeouts
docs.text:
• on_failure: fail (the default): a failing hook stops the job at its stage, before the next tofu step — at every stage, platform or repo. The run fails (audited run.check_failed). A failing before_apply hook means nothing is applied.
  • on_failure: warn: the job goes on and the warning is recorded. At a plan stage it forces the run to unconfirmed, even under autodeploy, so a human sees it (audited run.check_warned). At an apply stage the run is already confirmed: the apply goes on.
  • A failing after_apply hook fails the run although the apply has already changed the infrastructure. Stackd still records the new outputs and clears the environment's drift flag, but nothing cascades from a failed run.
  • Timeout. Each hook gets 10 minutes (STACKD_HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS on the worker). Past it the hook and every process it started are killed, and it fails by its own on_failure (detail timed out after <n>s).
  • No background process. When a hook's command exits, every process it left running in its process group (cmd &) is killed: nothing a hook starts outlives it. Run what a check needs in the foreground.
  • No plan JSON, no checks. If tofu can't produce the plan's JSON document, the plan job fails (plan JSON unavailable, not checked): an after_plan check never passes on an empty plan.

Tip

A warn check on after_plan is how you surface policy/cost findings without blocking — the run still stops for a human even under autodeploy.

docs.title: Check results
docs.text:
Every hook result is kept on the run, with the stage it ran at, across the plan and apply jobs: check_results in GET /api/v1/runs/{id} (or GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/checks).

"check_results": {
  "results": [
    {"name": "fmt",       "status": "ok",   "detail": null,     "stage": "before_plan"},
    {"name": "infracost", "status": "warn", "detail": "exit 1", "stage": "after_plan"}
  ],
  "checks": [
    {"name": "infracost", "status": "warn", "detail": "exit 1", "stage": "after_plan"}
  ]
}

results lists every check (ok, warn, fail), which the run page shows with each one's stage; checks only the ones that need attention. A job that fails on something other than a check (a tofu error, for example) still records the checks of the stages that ran, and a warning among them is audited.

docs.title: What hooks can see
docs.text:
A repo hook runs code that anyone who can open a pull request controls, so it gets nothing secret. A platform hook is trusted.

Platform hook Repo hook Process environment the worker's, minus the agent's own STACKD_* settings an allowlist of the worker's: PATH, HOME, locale, proxy and CA settings… Environment variables of the run all, sensitive ones included the non-sensitive ones Cloud credentials (OIDC) yes no plan.json at after_plan tofu's plan JSON as is a masked copy: every sensitive value is ***

Terraform variables reach no hook directly: tofu reads them from variable files that exist only while a tofu command runs (their values do show in plan.json, sensitive ones masked in a repo hook's copy). Give a hook what it needs as an environment variable.

While a repo hook runs, none of these is on disk: the saved plan, the run's variable files, the cloud token file, the repo token. Sensitive values are masked in every hook's output.

Not implemented yet

The specification also describes ignoring repo hooks at the *_apply stages of prod environments, and a per-environment opt-in giving repo hooks secrets or cloud credentials. Neither exists: repo hooks run at every stage, and never get secrets. The prod rule is pending a decision, since tiers are a configurable catalog. Until the container runner exists, hooks also run as the worker's own user, without isolation from other jobs on the same worker (SPECS §8.3).

docs.title: Managing platform hooks
docs.text:
Platform hooks are CRUD over the API, scoped to a stack or an environment:

curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/stacks/$STACK_ID/hooks -H "$AUTH" -d '{
  "stage": "after_plan", "name": "tfsec", "command": "tfsec .", "on_failure": "fail"
}'

docs.title: Importing an existing stack
docs.text: Already running Terraform with remote state? You can onboard it into Stackd two ways, depending on whether you want to keep your own backend or hand state over to Stackd.

docs.title: Path 1 — keep your backend (managed_state: false)
docs.text:
The zero-migration path. Set managed_state: false on the environment: Stackd injects nothing, your repo keeps its existing backend "s3" (or other) block, and Terraform keeps using your remote state exactly as before. Stackd still orchestrates the run (plan → approve → apply, audit, OIDC, cascade).

# create the env with managed state off
curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/stacks/$STACK_ID/environments -H "$AUTH" -d '{
  "name": "prod", "tier": "prod", "branch": "main", "managed_state": false
}'

The first plan reads your real state — a no-op diff confirms the import is correct before you apply anything.

Note

The worker reaches your backend with the per-run OIDC role, so that role must have access to your state bucket (and lock table, if any). You keep your own locking; you don't get Stackd's scoped state tokens / visible locking for this env.

docs.title: Path 2 — adopt Stackd-managed state (managed_state: true)
docs.text:
Hand state to Stackd (state in S3 behind its HTTP backend, per-job scoped tokens, visible locking, serial-regression guard). Migrate your current state once with a standard tofu init -migrate-state — Stackd hands you a scoped credential to do it.

1. Set the environment to managed state (managed_state: true).

2. Create an import session (admin) — mints a short-lived rw state token and a ready backend config:

curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/api/v1/environments/$ENV_ID/state/import-session -H "$AUTH"

{
  "expires_in": 1800,
  "current_serial": null,
  "backend": {
    "type": "http",
    "address": "https://stackd.example/state/v1/<env_id>",
    "lock_address": "https://stackd.example/state/v1/<env_id>/lock",
    "unlock_address": "https://stackd.example/state/v1/<env_id>/lock",
    "lock_method": "LOCK", "unlock_method": "UNLOCK",
    "username": "env", "password": "<scoped-token>"
  },
  "instructions": [ "..." ]
}

3. Migrate your state with the returned config. In a local checkout, switch the backend block to terraform { backend "http" {} }, then run once:

TF_HTTP_ADDRESS="$ADDRESS" \
TF_HTTP_LOCK_ADDRESS="$ADDRESS/lock" \
TF_HTTP_UNLOCK_ADDRESS="$ADDRESS/lock" \
TF_HTTP_LOCK_METHOD=LOCK \
TF_HTTP_UNLOCK_METHOD=UNLOCK \
TF_HTTP_USERNAME=env \
TF_HTTP_PASSWORD="$TOKEN" \
tofu init -migrate-state

The settings go through TF_HTTP_* environment variables rather than -backend-config: tofu writes -backend-config values, the token included, into .terraform/, while environment variables never touch disk. Stackd's own workers do the same.

Terraform LOCKs, uploads your current state through Stackd's backend (stored as a state_version), then UNLOCKs.

4. Remove the backend block from the committed code. On a managed-state environment the worker adds its own backend "http" {} block and hands the address and its job token to tofu through TF_HTTP_* environment variables, so the repo must declare no backend: a second backend block makes init fail. Future runs then use the managed backend automatically.

Clean up the local checkout

Delete the local .terraform/ once the migration is done, and don't commit the temporary backend "http" {} block (step 4).

Warning

The import session is admin-only, the token expires in 30 minutes, and creating it is audited (state.import_session_created). The endpoint refuses an env where managed_state is off (409). The returned addresses use STACKD_PUBLIC_URL, since you run tofu from your own machine.

In the local dev stack, the imported state lands in the Garage bucket that task dev provisions; task s3-ls lists it under states/<environment_id>/.

docs.title: Which to choose?
docs.text:
• Just want orchestration over your existing state? → Path 1 (managed_state: false). Instant.
  • Want Stackd to own state (scoped tokens, visible locking)? → Path 2, one init -migrate-state.
